newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Datacraft sees strong profit turnaround.
newsitem.headline: Datacraft sees strong profit turnaround.

text.p: Data communications equipment manufacturer Datacraft Ltd on Wednesday confirmed expectations of a strong profit turnaround in the current year to June 30, 1997.
Datacraft also said it was examining its capital structure so that its share price more closely reflected the value of its Asian investments.
"The directors of Datacraft Ltd are pleased to confirm expectations of a strong profit turnaround for the current financial year," Datacraft said.

"The earnings improvement will be driven by significant growth in Datacraft's Asian business which is expecting its profits to be 45 to 50 percent higher than the A$$8.5m profit earned in 1995/96 year, of which 55.3 percent is attributable to Datacraft Limited," it said.
Datacraft also said it expected its Australian businesses to return to profit this year, largely due to restructuring done in the last year.
"Also, the result will include an abnormal profit on the sale of its 50 percent share in Black Box Catalog Australia Pty Ltd."
Datacraft said its directors had highlighted recently that the price of Datacraft shares was significantly lower than the value per share of its investment in Datacraft Asia.
"Based upon the Datacraft Asia Ltd share price of A$2.90, the value per Datacraft Limited share of its investment in Datacraft Asia Ltd is A$2.72," Datacraft said.

"In view of this disparity between the Datacraft Limited share price and the market value of its investment in Datacraft Asia Limited and the continuing growth expectations of the Group, the Directors will focus their attentions on the future capital needs and structure of the Group."
Datacraft said it had engaged J.P. Morgan and Wentworth Associates as advisors to look at its capital structure.
Datacraft's shares closed up 25 cents at A$1.65 on Wednesday on volume of over 2.2 million shares traded.
